meta.disclaimer: These one-line region functions were written by an AI language model (LLM) and may be incomplete or wrong. Treat them as a rough orientation only and verify against primary sources (e.g. the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas and the literature).
meta.note: Keyed by Allen CCF acronym. A region without its own entry inherits the nearest parent structure's description, so broad divisions always provide a fallback.

fn.grey: Grey matter — neuronal cell bodies and local circuitry (as opposed to white-matter tracts).
fn.CH: Cerebrum — the cerebral hemispheres: neocortex and deep nuclei (basal ganglia, amygdala) for sensation, movement, cognition and emotion.
fn.BS: Brainstem — midbrain, pons and medulla: relays between brain and spinal cord, cranial-nerve nuclei, and nuclei controlling arousal and vital functions.
fn.Isocortex: Neocortex — the six-layered cerebral cortex for sensation, movement planning, perception and higher cognition.
fn.MO: Motor cortex — plans and commands voluntary movement.
fn.MOp: Primary motor cortex (M1) — drives voluntary movement; origin of much of the corticospinal tract.
fn.MOs: Secondary/premotor cortex (M2) — movement planning, preparation and sequencing (includes rodent frontal-orienting / eye-field-like regions).
fn.SS: Somatosensory cortex — represents touch and body sensation.
fn.SSp: Primary somatosensory cortex (S1) — maps touch across the body; in mouse contains the prominent whisker 'barrel' fields.
fn.SSs: Supplemental somatosensory cortex (S2) — higher-order touch processing.
fn.VIS: Visual cortical areas — hierarchical processing of visual information.
fn.VISp: Primary visual cortex (V1) — first cortical stage of vision; retinotopic processing of input relayed from the retina via the thalamus.
fn.AUD: Auditory cortex — processes sound frequency, timing and features.
fn.AUDp: Primary auditory cortex (A1) — tonotopic processing of sound.
fn.RSP: Retrosplenial cortex — spatial memory, navigation and head-direction coding; links hippocampal and neocortical networks.
fn.ACA: Anterior cingulate cortex — action–outcome evaluation, attention and cognitive/emotional control.
fn.PL: Prelimbic cortex (rodent medial prefrontal) — executive control, decision-making and goal-directed behaviour.
fn.ILA: Infralimbic cortex (rodent medial prefrontal) — regulation of emotional, autonomic and fear responses.
fn.ORB: Orbitofrontal cortex — represents value and supports flexible, outcome-based decisions.
fn.FRP: Frontal pole — most anterior prefrontal cortex; higher-order cognition and planning.
fn.AI: Insular / agranular insular cortex — interoception, taste and visceral signals, and emotional–autonomic integration.
fn.PTLp: Posterior parietal cortex — multisensory integration for spatial attention and sensorimotor transformation.
fn.TEa: Temporal association cortex — higher-order multisensory association.
fn.ECT: Ectorhinal cortex — temporal association cortex linked to perirhinal/entorhinal memory circuits.
fn.PERI: Perirhinal cortex — object recognition memory; gateway to the hippocampal formation.
fn.OLF: Olfactory areas — process the sense of smell.
fn.MOB: Main olfactory bulb — first relay for smell; mitral/tufted cells process odour input and project to olfactory cortex.
fn.AOB: Accessory olfactory bulb — processes pheromonal signals from the vomeronasal organ.
fn.AON: Anterior olfactory nucleus — early olfactory relay linking the two bulbs and olfactory cortex.
fn.PIR: Piriform (primary olfactory) cortex — identifies and represents odours.
fn.DP: Dorsal peduncular area — medial prefrontal/olfactory-related cortex.
fn.COA: Cortical amygdalar area — olfactory amygdala; links odour to emotional/behavioural responses.
fn.PAA: Piriform-amygdalar area — olfactory cortex bordering the amygdala.
fn.NLOT: Nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract — olfactory relay.
fn.HPF: Hippocampal formation — learning, episodic and spatial memory.
fn.HIP: Hippocampus — episodic and spatial memory; contains place cells.
fn.CA1: Hippocampal CA1 — main output stage of the hippocampus; episodic/spatial memory and place coding.
fn.CA2: Hippocampal CA2 — links CA3 and CA1; implicated in social memory.
fn.CA3: Hippocampal CA3 — recurrent network supporting memory recall and pattern completion.
fn.DG: Dentate gyrus — input stage of the hippocampus; pattern separation; a site of adult neurogenesis.
fn.SUB: Subiculum — major output of the hippocampus to cortical and subcortical targets; spatial processing.
fn.ProS: Prosubiculum — transition zone at the CA1–subiculum border; hippocampal output.
fn.ENT: Entorhinal cortex — gateway between neocortex and hippocampus; grid cells and spatial/memory coding.
fn.PAR: Parasubiculum — spatial/head-direction signals feeding the hippocampal formation.
fn.CTXsp: Cortical subplate — claustrum, endopiriform nucleus and amygdala.
fn.CLA: Claustrum — thin sheet with widespread reciprocal cortical connections; proposed role in coordinating cortical activity and attention.
fn.EP: Endopiriform nucleus — claustrum-associated region connected with olfactory and limbic cortex.
fn.LA: Lateral amygdala — sensory input gate of the amygdala; fear/threat learning.
fn.BLA: Basolateral amygdala — assigns emotional value to stimuli; fear and reward learning; interacts with cortex and hippocampus.
fn.BMA: Basomedial amygdala — emotional processing and regulation of fear/anxiety.
fn.CEA: Central amygdala — main output of the amygdala; drives autonomic and behavioural fear/defensive responses.
fn.MEA: Medial amygdala — processes social and pheromonal cues; reproductive and defensive behaviour.
fn.STR: Striatum — main input stage of the basal ganglia for action selection, reward and movement.
fn.CP: Caudoputamen (dorsal striatum) — integrates cortical and thalamic signals for action selection, habit and motor control; receives dopamine from the substantia nigra.
fn.ACB: Nucleus accumbens (ventral striatum) — limbic–motor interface for reward, motivation and reinforcement; receives dopamine from the VTA.
fn.OT: Olfactory tubercle — ventral striatal region linking olfaction, reward and motivation.
fn.LSX: Lateral septal complex — limbic region linking hippocampus and hypothalamus; emotion, reward and social behaviour.
fn.sAMY: Striatal amygdala (extended amygdala) — including BST-related circuits for stress, anxiety and motivated behaviour.
fn.PAL: Pallidum — output/relay nuclei of the basal ganglia and basal forebrain.
fn.GPe: External globus pallidus — GABAergic hub of the basal-ganglia indirect pathway; regulates movement.
fn.GPi: Internal globus pallidus / entopeduncular nucleus — GABAergic output of the basal ganglia to the motor thalamus.
fn.SI: Substantia innominata — basal forebrain; cholinergic and GABAergic neurons for cortical arousal, attention and motivation.
fn.MA: Magnocellular nucleus — basal forebrain cholinergic neurons; cortical activation and attention.
fn.NDB: Diagonal band nuclei — basal forebrain cholinergic/GABAergic projection to hippocampus and cortex; arousal and theta rhythm.
fn.MS: Medial septal nucleus — pacemaker of hippocampal theta rhythm; supports memory and spatial navigation.
fn.BST: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis — extended amygdala; sustained anxiety, stress and autonomic/neuroendocrine responses.
fn.TH: Thalamus — relays and gates sensory, motor and limbic signals to the cortex.
fn.VAL: Ventral anterior-lateral thalamus — motor relay carrying basal-ganglia and cerebellar output to motor cortex.
fn.VM: Ventral medial thalamus — motor thalamic nucleus with diffuse projection to superficial cortex; relays basal-ganglia/cerebellar output.
fn.VPM: Ventral posteromedial thalamus — somatosensory relay for the face/whiskers to primary somatosensory cortex.
fn.VPL: Ventral posterolateral thalamus — somatosensory relay for the body to primary somatosensory cortex.
fn.VP: Ventral posterior thalamus — somatosensory relay to cortex (face and body).
fn.LGd: Dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus — primary visual relay from the retina to primary visual cortex.
fn.LGv: Ventral lateral geniculate nucleus — visual region involved in circadian and oculomotor functions rather than image-forming vision.
fn.MG: Medial geniculate — auditory thalamic relay from the inferior colliculus to auditory cortex.
fn.MD: Mediodorsal thalamus — associative nucleus reciprocally linked with prefrontal cortex; cognition, working memory and decision-making.
fn.RT: Thalamic reticular nucleus — GABAergic shell that inhibits thalamic relay nuclei; gates thalamocortical transmission and shapes sleep spindles and attention.
fn.AV: Anteroventral thalamus — limbic (Papez) circuit; spatial memory and head-direction.
fn.AD: Anterodorsal thalamus — head-direction signals for navigation.
fn.AM: Anteromedial thalamus — limbic thalamic relay for memory and spatial cognition.
fn.LD: Laterodorsal thalamus — limbic relay for spatial learning and navigation.
fn.LP: Lateral posterior (pulvinar-like) thalamus — higher-order visual associative relay linking cortical areas.
fn.PO: Posterior thalamic nucleus — higher-order somatosensory relay (including whisker signals) linking cortical areas.
fn.PF: Parafascicular nucleus — intralaminar thalamus projecting to striatum and cortex; attention and arousal.
fn.CL: Central lateral nucleus — intralaminar thalamus; arousal, attention and cortical activation.
fn.CM: Central medial nucleus — intralaminar thalamus; arousal and cortical/striatal activation.
fn.RE: Nucleus reuniens — midline thalamus linking prefrontal cortex and hippocampus; memory and executive function.
fn.PVT: Paraventricular thalamus — midline nucleus signalling stress, arousal and salience to limbic targets.
fn.HY: Hypothalamus — homeostasis: feeding, drinking, temperature, hormones, circadian rhythm and motivated/defensive behaviour.
fn.PVH: Paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus — neuroendocrine and autonomic control; drives the stress (HPA) axis and oxytocin/vasopressin release.
fn.SO: Supraoptic nucleus — releases vasopressin and oxytocin for fluid balance and reproduction.
fn.ARH: Arcuate nucleus — senses hormones and controls feeding, energy balance and endocrine axes.
fn.VMH: Ventromedial hypothalamus — feeding, metabolism and defensive/aggressive behaviour.
fn.DMH: Dorsomedial hypothalamus — integrates feeding, circadian and stress signals for autonomic and behavioural output.
fn.LHA: Lateral hypothalamic area — arousal, feeding and motivated behaviour (orexin/MCH neurons).
fn.MPO: Medial preoptic area — thermoregulation, sleep and reproductive/parental behaviour.
fn.SCH: Suprachiasmatic nucleus — the master circadian clock, entrained by light.
fn.MM: Mammillary body — limbic memory circuit (Papez); relays hippocampal output to anterior thalamus.
fn.TU: Tuberal nucleus — hypothalamic region involved in feeding and social behaviour.
fn.ZI: Zona incerta — integrative subthalamic region modulating movement, arousal, pain and sensory gating.
fn.STN: Subthalamic nucleus — excitatory node of the basal-ganglia indirect/hyperdirect pathways; brakes movement (target in Parkinson's deep-brain stimulation).
fn.MB: Midbrain — sensory (visual/auditory) relays, orienting, dopaminergic and arousal systems, and motor control.
fn.SCs: Superior colliculus, sensory (superficial) layers — receive retinal and visual-cortical input to build a visual map.
fn.SCm: Superior colliculus, motor (deep) layers — multisensory layers commanding orienting of eyes, head and body (gaze).
fn.IC: Inferior colliculus — principal midbrain auditory relay; integrates ascending auditory input and projects to the medial geniculate.
fn.PAG: Periaqueductal gray — coordinates defensive behaviour, analgesia (descending pain control), vocalisation and autonomic responses.
fn.SNr: Substantia nigra pars reticulata — GABAergic output of the basal ganglia; tonically inhibits thalamus and superior colliculus to gate movement.
fn.SNc: Substantia nigra pars compacta — dopaminergic neurons projecting to the striatum (nigrostriatal pathway); essential for movement; degenerate in Parkinson's disease.
fn.VTA: Ventral tegmental area — dopaminergic neurons signalling reward and motivation; project to the accumbens and prefrontal cortex.
fn.RN: Red nucleus — midbrain motor nucleus; its magnocellular part gives rise to the rubrospinal tract influencing limb movement, and it relays cerebellar output.
fn.MRN: Midbrain reticular nucleus — reticular formation; arousal, movement and orienting.
fn.APN: Anterior pretectal nucleus — pretectum; pain modulation and visuomotor reflexes.
fn.PPT: Pedunculopontine nucleus — cholinergic locomotor/arousal centre; part of the mesencephalic locomotor region and reticular activating system.
fn.RR: Midbrain reticular nucleus, retrorubral area — contains dopaminergic neurons; motor and arousal functions.
fn.III: Oculomotor nucleus — motor neurons for most eye muscles and the pupil/lens.
fn.IV: Trochlear nucleus — motor neurons for the superior oblique eye muscle.
fn.P: Pons — bridges forebrain and cerebellum; relays cortical input to the cerebellum and houses arousal, sensory and autonomic nuclei.
fn.PG: Pontine gray (basal pontine nuclei) — major relay of cerebral cortical signals to the cerebellum, sent as mossy fibres to the contralateral cerebellar cortex.
fn.PRNc: Pontine reticular nucleus (caudal) — reticular formation; motor control, posture, startle and arousal/REM sleep.
fn.PRNr: Pontine reticular nucleus (rostral) — reticular formation; motor control, posture and arousal.
fn.TRN: Tegmental reticular nucleus — precerebellar relay conveying cortical and other signals to the cerebellum as mossy fibres.
fn.PB: Parabrachial nucleus — relays taste, visceral, thermal and pain signals; arousal and homeostasis.
fn.LC: Locus coeruleus — the main noradrenergic nucleus; arousal, attention, stress and brain-wide state modulation.
fn.DTN: Dorsal tegmental nucleus — part of the head-direction circuit for navigation.
fn.SLC: Subcoeruleus / pontine nucleus involved in REM-sleep atonia and arousal.
fn.PSV: Principal sensory nucleus of the trigeminal — relays facial touch, including whisker signals, to the thalamus and cerebellum.
fn.V: Motor trigeminal nucleus — motor neurons for the jaw/chewing muscles.
fn.VI: Abducens nucleus — motor neurons for the lateral rectus eye muscle (horizontal gaze).
fn.MY: Medulla — autonomic control (breathing, heart rate, blood pressure), reflexes, and sensory/motor cranial-nerve nuclei.
fn.IO: Inferior olivary complex — the sole source of climbing fibres to the cerebellum, signalling motor errors and timing; receives GABAergic nucleo-olivary input from the cerebellar nuclei, and its neurons are electrically coupled.
fn.VNC: Vestibular nuclei — process inner-ear balance signals for posture, gaze (vestibulo-ocular reflex) and spatial orientation; closely interconnected with the cerebellum.
fn.MV: Medial vestibular nucleus — balance and the vestibulo-ocular reflex; strongly linked with the cerebellum.
fn.LAV: Lateral vestibular nucleus (Deiters') — origin of the vestibulospinal tract controlling anti-gravity/extensor tone.
fn.SPIV: Spinal (inferior) vestibular nucleus — integrates vestibular and other sensory signals for balance.
fn.SUV: Superior vestibular nucleus — vestibulo-ocular reflex control.
fn.DCO: Dorsal cochlear nucleus — first central auditory relay; integrates auditory with somatosensory input.
fn.VCO: Ventral cochlear nucleus — first central auditory relay; preserves sound timing for localisation.
fn.CU: Cuneate nucleus — dorsal-column relay for fine touch and proprioception from the forelimb to the thalamus (and cerebellum).
fn.GR: Gracile nucleus — dorsal-column relay for fine touch and proprioception from the hindlimb/body.
fn.ECU: External cuneate nucleus — precerebellar relay of forelimb proprioception to the cerebellum as mossy fibres.
fn.LRN: Lateral reticular nucleus — precerebellar nucleus relaying spinal and brainstem signals to the cerebellum as mossy fibres.
fn.SPVO: Spinal trigeminal nucleus, oral part — facial touch and pain.
fn.SPVI: Spinal trigeminal nucleus, interpolar part — facial touch/pain including whisker signals; relays to thalamus and cerebellum.
fn.SPVC: Spinal trigeminal nucleus, caudal part — facial pain and temperature.
fn.NTS: Nucleus of the solitary tract — primary visceral and taste sensory nucleus; cardiorespiratory and gastrointestinal reflexes.
fn.AMB: Nucleus ambiguus — motor neurons for the pharynx/larynx (swallowing, vocalisation) and vagal control of the heart.
fn.XII: Hypoglossal nucleus — motor neurons controlling the tongue.
fn.DMX: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus — parasympathetic output to the viscera (heart, gut, lungs).
fn.GRN: Gigantocellular reticular nucleus — medullary reticular formation; premotor control of movement, posture and arousal.
fn.IRN: Intermediate reticular nucleus — medullary reticular formation; autonomic and motor coordination.
fn.MDRN: Medullary reticular nucleus — premotor and reticulospinal control of movement and posture.
fn.MARN: Magnocellular reticular nucleus — reticulospinal motor control and muscle tone.
fn.PARN: Parvicellular reticular nucleus — coordinates cranial-nerve motor output (e.g. orofacial movements).
fn.PGRN: Paragigantocellular reticular nucleus — autonomic (cardiovascular) and arousal control.
fn.AP: Area postrema — a circumventricular chemosensory organ that detects blood-borne signals and can trigger nausea/vomiting.
fn.RM: Nucleus raphe magnus — serotonergic; descending modulation of pain.
fn.RPA: Nucleus raphe pallidus — serotonergic; thermoregulation and autonomic control.
fn.RO: Nucleus raphe obscurus — serotonergic; motor and respiratory modulation.
fn.CB: Cerebellum — coordinates the timing, precision and learning of movement, contributes to balance and posture, and participates in cognitive and affective functions. It receives mossy-fibre input (via pontine and other precerebellar nuclei) and climbing-fibre input (from the inferior olive); its only output arises from the cerebellar nuclei.
fn.CBX: Cerebellar cortex — three layers (molecular, Purkinje, granular). Granule cells relay mossy-fibre input through parallel fibres to Purkinje cells, which also receive climbing fibres from the inferior olive; Purkinje cells form the inhibitory output of the cortex onto the cerebellar and vestibular nuclei.
fn.VERM: Cerebellar vermis — midline cerebellar cortex; posture, balance, locomotion and eye movements (projects mainly to the fastigial nucleus).
fn.HEM: Cerebellar hemisphere — lateral cerebellar cortex; coordination of limb movement and non-motor functions (projects to the interposed and dentate nuclei).
fn.CBN: Cerebellar nuclei — the main output of the cerebellum. Glutamatergic neurons excite premotor targets (thalamus, red nucleus, brainstem), while GABAergic nucleo-olivary neurons inhibit the inferior olive. They receive inhibitory Purkinje-cell input plus collaterals of mossy and climbing fibres.
fn.FN: Fastigial (medial) cerebellar nucleus — output nucleus for the vermis; posture, balance, locomotion and eye/head movements, via vestibular, reticular and thalamic projections.
fn.IP: Interposed cerebellar nucleus — output nucleus for the paravermis; limb coordination and feedback control of ongoing reaching movements; projects to the red nucleus and motor thalamus.
fn.DN: Dentate (lateral) cerebellar nucleus — output nucleus for the lateral hemisphere; timing and planning of movement and non-motor/cognitive functions; projects to motor and prefrontal thalamus and the red nucleus.
fn.FL: Flocculus — part of the vestibulocerebellum; controls the vestibulo-ocular reflex and gaze stabilisation.
fn.NOD: Nodulus — with the flocculus forms the vestibulocerebellum; processes vestibular signals for balance and the vestibulo-ocular reflex.
fn.fiber tracts: White-matter tract — a bundle of axons connecting brain regions, rather than a grey-matter area that processes signals locally.
fn.arb: Arbor vitae — the white matter of the cerebellum: the cerebellar peduncles and their branching tracts carrying input and output fibres.
fn.cbf: Cerebellar peduncles — the fibre tracts carrying all input to and output from the cerebellum.
fn.mcp: Middle cerebellar peduncle — carries pontine (corticopontine-relayed) mossy fibres into the cerebellum.
fn.scp: Superior cerebellar peduncle — the main output tract of the cerebellar nuclei to the thalamus and red nucleus (also carries some input).
fn.cm: Corticospinal / pyramidal-type motor tract — descending axons carrying motor commands toward the spinal cord.
fn.VS: Ventricular system — fluid-filled cavities containing cerebrospinal fluid; not neural tissue.
fn.V4: Fourth ventricle — CSF-filled cavity between the brainstem and cerebellum.
fn.VL: Lateral ventricle — CSF-filled cavity within each cerebral hemisphere.
